verdict: Broadridge's recurring revenue grew 11% as its investor-communications and capital-markets software kept expanding, but a $40M loss on digital assets cut GAAP EPS to $0.83.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenue was $1.7B, vs $1.6B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $1.40 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $1.56, +3%

kpis.label: Closed sales
kpis.note: +10% YoY — new contracts signed in the quarter

segments.name: Investor Communication Solutions
segments.note: Sending investors their proxy votes, statements and disclosures for banks, brokers and funds. Recurring revenue rose 10% to $568M and distribution revenue (mostly postage pass-through) rose 4% to $518M, but one-off event-driven revenue fell 41% to $67M on fewer mutual-fund proxies.

segments.name: Global Technology & Operations
segments.note: Software and processing for capital markets, wealth and investment managers — all recurring revenue, up 12%, with capital-markets revenue up 17% including the CQG acquisition.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company — up 9% YoY on higher revenue-related and technology costs and recent acquisitions.

otherDetail: Costs below operating profit were $64M, net: $27M of net interest expense plus $37M of other non-operating expense, which mainly reflects a $40M loss on digital assets (see one-time items).
footerNote: Broadridge reports in one decimal place ($1,668.7M of revenue); figures here are rounded to whole $M and the GTO segment is shown at $516M (release: $515.5M) so the lines tie exactly. Its tax rate was an unusually low 13.6% this quarter because of discrete tax benefits.
oneTimers: A $40M loss on digital assets (mainly mark-to-market on its Canton-related holdings), versus a $46M gain a year ago — an $86M year-over-year swing in pre-tax profit, reported in Corporate and Other.
Restructuring and other related costs of $15M — severance tied in part to AI and productivity initiatives.
Amortization of acquired intangibles and purchased intellectual property of $39M, plus $2M of acquisition and integration costs.
Excluding these items, adjusted net earnings were $178M ($1.56 per share, +3%) versus GAAP net earnings of $95M ($0.83).

takeaways.title: The subscription core is healthy
takeaways.text: Recurring revenue — the contracted, repeat business — rose 11% to $1,083M, 9 points of it organic. Closed sales of new contracts rose 10% to $36M, and full-year guidance was reaffirmed.

takeaways.title: One-off proxy work shrank
takeaways.text: Event-driven revenue fell 41% to $67M because there were fewer mutual-fund proxy campaigns — the lumpy part of the business. That, not the core, is why total revenue grew only 5% and ICS pre-tax earnings fell 18% to $104M.

takeaways.title: A digital-asset loss cut GAAP EPS
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS fell 41% to $0.83, mostly on the $40M digital-asset loss versus a $46M gain a year ago. Adjusted EPS, which leaves that out, rose 3% to $1.56. Broadridge also bought back $200M of stock and paid $111M of dividends.
